'''David Nualart''' (born 21 March 1951)<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://nualart.ku.edu/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae for David Nualart|publisher=University of Kansas|access-date=2024-05-17}}</ref> is a Spanish mathematician working in the field of [[probability theory]], in particular on aspects of [[stochastic process]]es and [[stochastic analysis]]. He is retired as Black-Babcock Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Kansas]].

==Education and career==
Nualart obtained his PhD titled "Contribución al estudio de la integral estocástica" in 1975 at the [[University of Barcelona]] under the supervision of Francesc d'Assís Sales Vallès.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|93562}}</ref> After positions at the [[University of Barcelona]] and the [[Polytechnique University of Barcelona]] he took up a professorship at the [[University of Kansas]] and was the Black-Babcock Distinguished Professor in its Mathematics Department from 2012 to 2022.<ref name=cv/> He retired in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.ku.edu/news/article/2022/05/04/ku-honor-faculty-academic-staff-retirees|title=KU to honor faculty, academic staff retirees|work=KU News|publisher=University of Kansas|date=4 May 2022|access-date=2024-05-17}}</ref>

He was the Chief Editor of [[Electronic Communications in Probability]] from 2006 to 2008.<ref name=cv/>

==Recognition==
He has been elected a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics in 1997.
He received a Doctor Honoris Causa by the [[Université Blaise Pascal]] of Clermond-Ferrand in 1998.
He received the Prize IBERDROLA de Ciencia y Tecnologia in 1999.
He has been a Corresponding Member of the Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas Fisicas y Naturales of
Madrid since 2003.
He has been a member of the Reial Academia de Ciencies i Arts of Barcelona since 2003.
He received the Research Prize of the Real Academia de Ciencias de Madrid in 1991.<ref name=cv/>

In March 2011 the International Conference on [[Malliavin Calculus]] and Stochastic Analysis in honor of David
Nualart took place at [[University of Kansas]]. The results were published in 2013 as a [[festschrift]], ''Malliavin Calculus and Stochastic Analysis: A Festschrift in Honor of David Nualart''.<ref>{{MR|3155263}}; {{zbl|1261.60005}}</ref>

He was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to Malliavin calculus, stochastic PDE's, and fractional Brownian motion".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2023 Class of Fellows|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2022-11-09|archive-date=2022-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109214706/https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|url-status=dead}}</ref>
